$comment: Prerequisite edges. hard gates the knowledge frontier; this graph currently uses hard edges only, one per topic, forming a single chain from the one entry point (mt_api_request_structure), matching the style of learning-graph/section-07.

dependencies.reason: The roles are what populate the messages array this topic's request shape defines.
stop_reason describes how an assistant turn ends, so reading it presupposes knowing which role produces that turn.
The context window is built from the same messages array; its failure modes only make sense once you know what's accumulating inside it.
tool_use is one of the four stop_reason values — the mechanism can't be explained without the signal that announces it.
Description-driven selection only matters once a tool call is understood as a structured request the model chooses to emit.
tool_choice controls whether and which tool_use happens, so it presupposes what tool_use is.
Schema design shapes a tool_use call's input_schema, and syntax/semantic errors are properties of that same call.
The loop's only branch point is checking stop_reason for tool_use versus end_turn.
AgentDefinition configures which loop an agent runs — system_prompt and allowed_tools only matter against that loop.
A coordinator and its subagents are each just an AgentDefinition with a different allowed_tools list.
The Task tool is how the hub actually spawns a spoke — it only makes sense against that topology.
Hooks intercept specific points in the same loop — PreToolUse and PostToolUse are loop steps.
MCP tools reach the model through the same tool_use mechanism; MCP is a way of supplying more of them.
Configuring a server presupposes knowing what a server provides.
isError is a field on a specific MCP tool's response, so the tool/resource/server model comes first.
Resources are one of the three primitives the MCP overview introduces.
CLAUDE.md behaves like a persistent, layered system prompt — the system role has to be understood first.
@path exists only to keep the CLAUDE.md hierarchy from duplicating content across its levels.
.claude/rules/ is presented as an alternative organization to the same hierarchy.
Commands and skills are contrasted against CLAUDE.md's always-loaded model — on-demand versus always-on is the point.
Planning mode changes what the agentic loop is allowed to do — investigate only, or investigate and act.
/compact is the built-in mitigation for the exact summarization-loss problem that topic describes.
Headless CI execution is direct execution taken to its extreme — no human ever sees a plan to approve.
The format-normalization rules here are the free-text extension of the same nullable/enum discipline schema design teaches.
Explicit criteria make explicit the rule an example was only demonstrating implicitly.
Each link in a chain is only reliable if it's given the same explicit, non-vague criteria this topic argues for.
Asking clarifying questions is how you obtain explicit criteria when the requester hasn't supplied them yet.
Retry-with-feedback is the runtime backstop for exactly the semantic errors schema design cannot prevent.
A batch request is a list of the same params object Chapter 1 defines, submitted asynchronously instead of one at a time.
custom_id and failure handling are mechanics of the same batch object the overview introduces.
Planning a submission window presupposes knowing how failures get identified and resubmitted within it.
Fixed pipelines and dynamic decomposition are the same fixed-vs-adaptive split, generalized from a prompt chain to a whole task plan.
Multi-pass review is a fixed pipeline — per-file passes then an integration pass — worked through as a concrete example.
Reliable triggers are the deterministic-rule side of the hooks-vs-prompts split, applied to when a human takes over.
Deciding when and how to escalate only makes sense once what counts as a trigger is settled.
The handoff protocol is what the agent hands the human once one of these escalation patterns has fired.
Confidence-based routing is the alternative the triggers topic offers in place of the unreliable self-rated-confidence trigger it rules out.
The error taxonomy generalizes the single isError flag into the transient/validation/business/permission split multi-agent systems need.
Each anti-pattern is a specific mishandling of one of the categories just defined.
The structured-error shape is what the anti-patterns topic argues you replace a generic status with.
A dedicated facts block is a direct countermeasure for the progressive-summarization data loss this topic describes.
Both apply the same discipline — keep only what's load-bearing in context — first to derived facts, then to raw tool output.
Once results are trimmed to what matters, where that surviving content sits in the prompt is the next lever.
A scratchpad is where position-aware, load-bearing findings get written down so they survive outside the prompt entirely.
Structured state files generalize a single scratchpad into a manifest coordinating several agents' saved progress.
Coverage annotations already track which parts of a synthesis are trustworthy; provenance tracks where each individual claim inside it came from.
You can only detect a conflict between two sources if each value already carries the attribution the previous topic argues for.
A date is often the fact that resolves an apparent conflict into an explainable trend instead of a contradiction.
Incremental Grep-then-Read investigation is what planning mode's read-only phase actually does, tool by tool.
The fallback only comes up once Edit has been chosen and attempted as part of that same investigation-driven workflow.
